question: Does representation capacity, source-deal coverage, label noise, or optimization block distillation of the lawful T0 teacher into a cheap net? Capacity is a candidate, not a default.
inherited: teacher T0 = all-action Q under frozen P-1 uniform legal play for every future actor; belief = uniform over capacity-compatible hidden completions given own hand and legal public history (support-conditioned surrogate, NOT the gameplay posterior); raw 862 information-set encoding; kernel.c byte-identical to both prior experiments; fixed bid 30, pip trump 0..6, no bidding model.
prior_diagnosis: On the committed coverage validation panel the prior nets mixed32/late32/late64 reach held-out scaled centered-advantage MSE .1476/.1477/.1485 against a zero-predictor MSE .1491 and a 128-world sampling floor of about .004: held-out R^2 about 1%. Training loss falls to <.01. This is a generalization failure at 3,648 roots, not a fit failure; it motivates a learning curve in source deals crossed with capacity.

sources.roots_per_deal: at most one live nonforced root per absolute-ply band 0-7/8-15/16-23, chosen uniformly by the per-deal trajectory RNG among unique information sets
sources.exclusion: all source partitions of both prior experiments and all prior phone-game deals; all prior actor-normalized inputs; duplicates across this experiment keep first occurrence; test roots duplicating any train root are dropped

validation: the committed coverage experiment validation panel: 1,024 roots (256/256/512 early/mid/late) over 256 deals, reference0 4,096-world Q and teacher128 labels (coverage batches 012-013). Used for checkpoint selection and validation reporting only.

d1.note: first v source deals of the frozen train sequence

d4.note: first v source deals of the frozen train sequence

d16.note: first v source deals of the frozen train sequence

feat-s64.kind: per-action feature scorer with shared MLP over 32 lawful features

features: 32 per-action features computed only from own current hand, public ordered plays, trump, bidder, leader, public scores: trump/double/count/pips, universe rank in context, follows/leading, wins current trick, unseen tiles that beat it, unseen followers, own followers, master flag, own higher, players after, partner played/winning/after, opponent winning, table points, partner/opponent revealed voids in context, unseen/own trumps, team bidding, scores, tricks remaining, hand size, bidder/defender points needed, unseen count, legal count. No hidden hands, no source identity, no labels.

optimizer.init: first raw layer std .08, hidden std sqrt(2/fan_in), output std .04*sqrt(32/fan_in), zero bias, NumPy seed 12345
optimizer.selection: minimum validation scaled centered-advantage MSE against the 4,096-world validation reference, evaluated every 50 updates; validation regret is recorded, not used for selection
optimizer.budget_note: identical maximum update budget for every arm; selected update count and whether selection hit the final evaluation are reported; an arm that selects within the last 10% of the budget is flagged budget-limited

trainings.secondary_reg: raw-h256-reg-d1 = raw-h256 at d1 with lr .0005 and l2 1e-3 as a single optimization/regularization check

hypotheses.H_capacity_at_prior_scale: at d1, raw-h256 and raw-d256 do not have paired upper 95% bound < 0 against raw-h32 on fresh test regret (capacity alone does not unblock)
hypotheses.H_coverage: raw-h32 at d16 has paired upper 95% bound < 0 against raw-h32 at d1 on fresh test regret (source-deal coverage is a blocker)
hypotheses.H_capacity_x_data: at d16, raw-d256 versus raw-h32 paired difference; direction not preregistered, reported
hypotheses.H_representation: feat-s64 at d1 versus raw-h32 at d1 paired; feat-s64 at d16 versus raw-d256 at d16 paired; secondary
hypotheses.noise: bounded, not retested: the 128-world scaled sampling floor is about .004 against a .149 zero-predictor MSE; the prior subset512 control showed no decision gain

metrics: regret = max_a Q_ref(a) - Q_ref(chosen) in acting-partnership contract-win probability under the stated surrogate teacher, all-band and late-band; equal-weight means per source deal; 5,000-draw source-deal bootstrap; best-set and resolved (gap > 3 paired SE, heuristic) agreement; held-out R^2 of scaled centered advantage; warm CPU latency (network-only, validated decision); parameters and bytes; training and label wall seconds. Not multiplicity corrected. Teacher-relative, not optimal-game regret.
rung: no frozen-policy rung is run in this phase under any outcome; the rung decision returns to Jason with the diagnosis
resources: every invocation under run_capped.py <= 295 s process-group cap; at most two concurrent label workers; local MLX Metal only; no cloud, no installs, no transmissions, no production, no fixture export

amendments.stage: before any freeze; test roots unmined and unlabeled
amendments.change: eval_every 50 -> 10 updates for every arm; selection rule (minimum validation MSE) unchanged; max_updates unchanged
amendments.reason: at d1 (about 18 updates per epoch) all three raw arms selected the first evaluation at update 50 with validation MSE already rising, so a 50-update grid cannot resolve the early minimum; the prior experiments selected at epoch 2 (about 30 updates). A finer grid applies equally to every arm.
amendments.retained: the three coarse-grid runs are archived under results/pre-amendment-eval50/ (raw-h32-d1 .10137, raw-h256-d1 .10616, raw-d256-d1 .10870 validation MSE at update 50) and are not used for any claim

amendments.stage: after validation results of the frozen-rule arms were read; before freeze; test roots unmined and unlabeled
amendments.change: add regret-selected copies rs-<arm>.regret for the nine primary arms and the three feat-s64 arms: identical training (same seed, data, budget) re-run with --also-regret, which additionally saves the checkpoint with minimum validation regret on the 10-update grid. The MSE-selected weights of each re-run are hash-compared with the frozen-rule arm as a determinism receipt.
amendments.reason: validation curves show validation MSE reaching its minimum within the first few hundred updates while validation regret keeps falling for thousands of updates on the larger raw nets (e.g. raw-h256-d16 MSE-selected regret .0314 at update 240 versus a history minimum .0255 at update 5760). The preregistered MSE selector therefore confounds the capacity comparison with a selection-objective mismatch. Regret selection over 600 checkpoints on the same validation panel is optimistic by construction; these arms are labeled post hoc and secondary, and the fresh test is the only unbiased read.
amendments.status: secondary, post hoc on validation, declared before test
